Sub-theme 'Grid-connected PV: performance and techno-economics in buildings, campuses and utility plants' of group 1: 27 studies, cite as \cite{R0013,R0034,R0049,R0054,R0062,R0068,R0095,R0143,R0165,R0249,R0321,R0329,R0335,R0348,R0409,R0423,R0452,R0531,R0543,R0920,R1168,R1192,R1223,R1401,R1439,R1631,R1780}. Methods: techno-economic assessment 16; empirical case study 7; modelling/simulation 3; other 1. Settings: sectors: buildings-residential 13; buildings-commercial-institutional 5; power-generation-SIN 4; multi-sector 4 | departments: Bogotá D.C. 9; Atlántico 5; Antioquia 3; Santander 3; La Guajira 2; none stated 3. Technical outcomes: performance ratio 86.22% base to 90.36% with bifacial modules at albedo 0.4 [R0013]; module efficiency 15.73% poly vs 17.05% mono in Bogotá [R0249]; module efficiency 12.45% monocrystalline, 11.04% polycrystalline, 6.32% amorphous in Pasto [R0531]; campus performance ratio 0.73-0.78 [R0335]; micro-inverters raise performance ratio 5.9% (no shade) and 8% (shaded) [R0068]; reflective surface +9.94% and combined cooling/reflection +13.8% daily energy [R0143]; PVsyst performance ratio 84.2% [R0095]; north campus carport supplied 1.7% of campus demand [R0335]. Economic outcomes: IRR 18.31% and payback 5.21 years for the bifacial farm at albedo 0.4 [R0013]; IRR 20.74% in Barranquilla (3.5 kWp) and 16.22% in Bogota [R0034]; IRR 19.67%, payback 7 years (Santander) [R0165]; IRR 31.3%, payback 4.7 years (Bogotá) [R1223]; IRR 9.1%, payback 8.5 years (Medellin) [R0452]; LCOE 0.240 vs 0.257 USD/kWh micro-inverter vs string [R0068]; LCOE 0.10 USD/kWh vs Putumayo tariff 0.17 [R1401]; payback 10.2 (levels 1-2) to 6.0 years (Bogota) [R0409]; payback exceeds 9 years, about 20 in stratum 1 [R0920]; payback 7-15 years by stratum [R1192]; IRR 11.05% and 13-year payback for a yard-based bus-fleet PV plant [R1780]; storage only profitable with price drops (11.26% IRR at 25% lower storage price) [R0034]; no residential scenario viable at the 0.1468 USD/kWh scarcity price [R0329]. Environmental outcomes: avoided CO2 about 20.4 t in 25 years [R0095]; 117.8 kgCO2e/yr avoided [R1223]; 346 kg CO2 avoided per 2 kW system [R0409]; about 193 kgCO2/yr saved per household [R0452]; avoided CO2 by 2050 Bogota 7,106.51 t [R0348]; 42.3 t CO2/yr avoided at a hospital [R1168]; CO2 avoided 0.15 t in 30-day monitoring [R0049]; construction is the most critical phase of a utility plant, with severe negative impacts on flora, fauna and landscape [R0423]. Pattern: Residential PV pays back within roughly 5 to 10 years for higher strata and favourable tariffs (R0165, R1223, R0452, R0409) but fails or needs a subsidy in strata 1-3 (R0920, R0329), so financial viability depends on stratum and tariff more than on technology; technical studies (R0249, R0531, R0068, R0143) report single-site gains that are not comparable across sites. (Values are the extracted values; each bracketed record id is the study reporting that value and is cited as \cite{<id>}.)

Sub-theme 'Solar policy, diffusion and power-system integration' of group 1: 19 studies, cite as \cite{R0057,R0104,R0115,R0140,R0200,R0230,R0278,R0382,R0400,R0462,R0463,R0464,R0472,R0479,R0505,R0517,R0853,R1321,R1840}. Methods: modelling/simulation 12; literature review 3; policy analysis 2; techno-economic assessment 2. Settings: sectors: power-generation-SIN 10; buildings-residential 5; multi-sector 3; non-interconnected-zones 1 | departments: Antioquia 3; Chocó 1; La Guajira 1; Bolívar 1; Córdoba 1; none stated 13. Technical outcomes: rooftop PV 4,400-10,600 MW by 2035 [R0104]; about 7532 MW PV by 2040 under FIT and subsidy, 7029 MW under net metering [R0115]; 1542 MW installed PV by 2030 vs 1090 MW in UPME expansion plan [R0278]; 1, 2 and 3 kW households give 2.5, 11 and 16 GW PV by 2035 [R0382]; PV adoption converges to 25-30% of households [R0200]; about 6 million adopter households by 2027 [R0517]; 5.82 MW by 2035 under the aggressive scheme [R0505]; distributed PV has no major impact on distribution costs at up to 31.8% penetration [R0472]; harmonic limits exceeded at 9th-12th harmonics [R0479]; node hosting capacity up to 6,071 kW and as low as 1,380 kW [R1321]; about 5.28 MW PV installed [R0464]; current solar power 7,036 MW [R0462]. Economic outcomes: net metering most efficient (20,298 USD/MW), capital subsidy least efficient (509,616 USD/MW) [R0115]; Law 1715 reduces LCOE by 16% to 33% (231.36 USD/MWh baseline to as low as 154.86) [R0463]; household tariff rises 0.13 to 0.20 USD/kWh [R0104]; tariffs for non-PV households rise about 20% by 2040 [R0200]; grid tariffs rise to 0.37 USD/kWh [R0517]; at 3 kW utilities recover 0% of costs, and net billing restores 100% cost recovery [R0382]; mean NPV rises from -2.55 to 3.45 MUSD with the fiscal incentive [R1840]; IRR 30.47% and 4-year payback for the large-scale scenario [R0278]; minimum FiT to start diffusion USD 0.30/kWh [R0505]; urban EMS daily savings USD 2711.57 (27.30%) [R0400]. Environmental outcomes: avoided 71.9 t CO2 on a campus [R0057]; urban 3472.28 kg CO2 (27.69%) and rural 6019.45 kg CO2 (35.38%) daily reductions with EMS [R0400]; emission reduction 6.7% in the BAV scenario [R0853]. Pattern: Simulation studies agree that unmanaged residential PV diffusion raises tariffs for non-adopters and erodes utility cost recovery (R0104, R0200, R0382, R0517), but disagree on diffusion size (25-30% of households in R0200 vs about 6 million households in R0517), and installed-capacity figures differ widely between reviews (R0464 vs R0462). (Values are the extracted values; each bracketed record id is the study reporting that value and is cited as \cite{<id>}.)

Sub-theme 'Off-grid, solar-thermal and productive-use solar applications' of group 1: 29 studies, cite as \cite{R0032,R0035,R0065,R0077,R0082,R0099,R0116,R0132,R0155,R0156,R0188,R0195,R0222,R0245,R0262,R0298,R0332,R0333,R0387,R0402,R0415,R0451,R0623,R0641,R0961,R1141,R1309,R1437,R1584}. Methods: empirical case study 8; modelling/simulation 9; techno-economic assessment 5; qualitative social study 3; other 2; policy analysis 1; literature review 1. Settings: sectors: non-interconnected-zones 10; multi-sector 6; buildings-residential 4; agriculture 4 | departments: Antioquia 5; La Guajira 5; Meta 3; Bolívar 3; Atlántico 2; none stated 4. Technical outcomes: Inírida solar farm supplies 10-30% of daytime demand [R0961]; Mitú 47 kWp system reliability above 90% [R0961]; solar home system performance ratio 0.77 (Case-1) and 0.95 with load shifting [R1309]; direct-expansion solar heat pump annual COP about 3.5, solar fraction above 88% [R0451]; parabolic trough reaches the 69-79 C range with 5 m2 [R0155]; 76.6 MWt parabolic-trough plant supplies 37.5% of daily steam, capacity factor 44.87% [R0195]; cocoa drying time fell to under 22 h [R0082]; hybrid solar gas-turbine efficiency 35% without solar input falling to 30% at midday [R0623]; solar RO desalination pumping energy 5.91 kWh/m3 [R0333]; renewable fraction above 98% [R1584]. Economic outcomes: LCOH below 0.075 USD/kWh [R0451]; LCOE 0.05546 $/kWh and CAPEX US$560/kW for solar-thermal steam [R0195]; IRR 18-24% and payback 5-6 years for San Andrés PV [R1437]; IRR 2% and payback 4 years for a portable solar water machine [R0116]; payback 5 years without batteries vs 14 and 9 years with batteries [R0099]; agrivoltaics IRR 7-9%, payback 13-14 years [R1141]; IRR 9.88% (PVES) vs 2.06% (CE) in tilapia farming [R0222]; STESS capex USD 22,711, about 30 times the USD 738 of conventional heaters [R0332]; COE 83-199 EUR/MWh [R1584]; diesel electricity costs USD 0.26/kWh [R0245]; 18% lower generation cost at Inírida [R0961]; PV prototypes cut energy supply cost by about 15% [R0402]. Environmental outcomes: about 2,970 t CO2 per year avoided at Inírida [R0961]; about 916.2 kg CO2/year avoided per house [R0245]; 81,645.78 g CO2 saved per year [R0035]; PV-powered UV/H2O2 removed anthracene and benzo[a]pyrene with efficiencies near 100% [R0099]; environmental impacts mostly very low, landscape medium [R1437]. Pattern: Off-grid and productive-use solar is technically workable and displaces diesel (R0961, R1309, R0245), but economics split by application: PV for diesel-dependent or consumer-bill uses reaches IRR 18-24% (R1437) while niche productive uses fall to IRR 2% (R0116) or need batteries that lengthen payback to 14 years (R0099), and solar-thermal evidence (R0155, R0195, R0451) rests on simulation only. (Values are the extracted values; each bracketed record id is the study reporting that value and is cited as \cite{<id>}.)

Sub-theme 'Onshore and small wind: resource, grid integration, economics and barriers' of group 1: 20 studies, cite as \cite{R0083,R0127,R0133,R0265,R0366,R0378,R0384,R0443,R0445,R0470,R0493,R0591,R0772,R0799,R1054,R1070,R1201,R1219,R1345,R1535}. Methods: modelling/simulation 10; empirical case study 3; qualitative social study 2; other 2; policy analysis 1; techno-economic assessment 1; literature review 1. Settings: sectors: power-generation-SIN 16; non-interconnected-zones 2; industry 1; buildings-residential 1 | departments: La Guajira 3; Bolívar 2; Nariño 2; Atlántico 1; Boyacá 1; none stated 12. Technical outcomes: mean wind speed 4.4 m/s at 10 m [R0772]; annual means 2.5-3.5 m/s at 10 m and about 5 m/s at 50 m in Soledad [R0366]; mean wind speed about 1.5 m/s, wind judged not viable in Barrios Unidos [R1201]; mean wind speeds 12-13 m/s La Guajira [R1345]; capacity factors 1.2-34.2% after losses across five sites [R0445]; wind capacity only 19.5 MW [R0378]; VAWT Cp 0.15-0.35 [R0127]; six small turbines net generation 467.6 MWh/yr [R0493]; 474 MW wind avoids 250 MW of coal [R0591]; grid limits wind to 210-440 MW without reinforcement vs 1,200 MW with second 500 kV link [R0591]; maximum active power ramp 140 MW/min [R0470]; system inertia falls about 12% [R0470]; 28,849 MW wind by 2050 in Green Democracy [R0083]. Economic outcomes: operating cost 985.43 MUSD without wind vs 764.17 MUSD (Case A), savings 22.6% [R0443]; mean cost 111,849 to 91,305 COP/MWh from 0 to 1,000 MW [R1219]; marginal cost reduced by about 1.2 US$/MWh, B/C 1.4 [R0591]; IRR 50.69% and NPV EUR 726,686 for chiller-airflow small wind [R0493]; wind share 31.0% in the minimum-volatility portfolio [R0384]; nano-turbine estimated cost one third of commercial value [R0799]. Environmental outcomes: avoided emissions 1.2 Mt (vs hydro) and 149.7 Mt CO2e (vs coal) [R0083]; 300 tCO2/yr avoided [R0493]; 54 wind parks and 2,168 turbines by 2030 (about 45 thousand ha) [R1070]; Wayuu are 42.2% of department population [R1070]; Villa Teresa 34.16% CF but exclusionary environmental limits [R0445]. Pattern: Studies agree wind lowers system operating cost and spot price (R0443, R1219, R0591) while grid and inertia constraints bind (R0470, R0591), but the resource evidence conflicts (12-13 m/s in La Guajira in R1345 vs 2.5-3.5 m/s at Soledad in R0366 and about 1.5 m/s in Bogotá in R1201), and only 19.5 MW is installed (R0378), so the benefit estimates remain model-based. (Values are the extracted values; each bracketed record id is the study reporting that value and is cited as \cite{<id>}.)

Sub-theme 'Offshore wind in the Caribbean: resource, siting, cost and floating platforms' of group 1: 11 studies, cite as \cite{R0336,R0367,R0966,R0990,R1161,R1397,R1402,R1442,R1473,R1500,R1543}. Methods: modelling/simulation 5; literature review 2; techno-economic assessment 2; empirical case study 1; other 1. Settings: sectors: power-generation-SIN 11 | departments: La Guajira 9; Atlántico 7; Bolívar 5; Magdalena 5; Antioquia 1; none stated 1. Technical outcomes: La Guajira WPD 796 W/m2 and Cf 61.5% [R1543]; Bolívar WPD 511 W/m2 and Cf 41.7% [R1543]; 360 MW farm capacity factor ~37% [R1161]; La Guajira 482 W/m2 (110.8 m) and Barranquilla 857 W/m2 [R0367]; Gulf of Urabá power density 33.59-128.39 W/m2 [R0990]; mean annual wind speed above 10 m/s in the north [R1397]; five feasible zones with wind speeds 8.2-10.9 m/s [R1500]; offshore technical potential about 110 GW [R1473]; reference wind year mean speed 6.98 vs 7.01 m/s [R1442]; lowest wind speed 2.403 m/s [R0336]; maximum sway 2.8 m under extreme sea state [R1402]. Economic outcomes: La Guajira CAPEX USD 1.202 billion (lowest), Bolívar USD 1.713 billion [R1543]; Atlántico and Magdalena CAPEX USD 5.156 billion each [R1543]; OPEX about USD 103 million/yr [R1543]; LCOE 12.3 cents/kWh and NPV $103,433,664 for a 360 MW farm [R1161]. Environmental outcomes: protected areas weight 19.62% [R1473]; protected areas weight 19.59% [R1500]; six stations rejected for marine protected areas [R1397]. Pattern: Offshore studies agree the northern Caribbean is the strongest and cheapest site (R1543, R1397, R1500), but resource figures conflict (La Guajira 482 W/m2 in R0367 vs 796 W/m2 in R1543, and R1161 ranks Barranquilla above La Guajira), and protected areas are the heaviest siting constraint (R1473, R1500). (Values are the extracted values; each bracketed record id is the study reporting that value and is cited as \cite{<id>}.)

Sub-theme 'Ocean energy: wave, tidal, salinity-gradient and OTEC' of group 1: 14 studies, cite as \cite{R0174,R0190,R0238,R0326,R0327,R0383,R0509,R1194,R1336,R1387,R1497,R1507,R1547,R1561}. Methods: modelling/simulation 9; techno-economic assessment 2; empirical case study 2; literature review 1. Settings: sectors: power-generation-SIN 8; non-interconnected-zones 6 | departments: Valle del Cauca 4; Atlántico 2; Chocó 2; La Guajira 1; San Andrés y Providencia 1; none stated 5. Technical outcomes: salinity gradient net power about 6 MW for 30 m3/s [R0174]; membrane power density 6.45 W/m2 [R0174]; membrane power density up to 6.4 W/m2 [R0326]; salinity gradient technical potential 780 MW [R0190]; base case 780 MW installed by 2046 [R0327]; OWC maximum chamber efficiency 67.2% [R1194]; OWC maximum chamber efficiency 66.81% [R1561]; wave converter average electric power 1.17 kW (regular) and 0.5 kW (irregular) [R1336]; maximum wave power above 25 kW/m [R0383]; Buenaventura mean velocities 0.28-0.54 m/s, max 1.36 m/s [R1387]; tidal velocities 0.25-1 m/s, maxima up to 2.2 m/s [R1497]; tidal barrage mean about 130.7 MW, 24 turbines of 5.45 MW [R1507]; 10 MW OTEC plant about 80 GWh/yr [R0509]. Economic outcomes: LCOE solar 46, wind 71, wave 306, tidal 196, current 594 USD/MWh [R0238]; LCOE about 62 USD/MWh for reverse electrodialysis [R0327]; pumping 6% of costs [R0174]; pretreatment up to 54% of potential [R0327]; 75% cheaper pretreatment with doubled permeability gives 19 MW [R0174]. Environmental outcomes: linear array cut beach-face erosion about 20% vs about 12% for semicircular layouts [R0383]; GHG reduction 95% for all technologies, tidal 342,043 tCO2/year [R0238]; about 13,000 m3/day desalinized water with OTEC [R0509]. Pattern: Salinity-gradient estimates agree on membrane power density near 6.4 W/m2 (R0174, R0326) and on a large potential (780 MW in R0190, R0327), whereas wave and tidal evidence (R1194, R1561, R1336, R1387, R1497) is simulation or laboratory scale, and only R0238 and R0327 give costs, so economic comparison across ocean options is not supported. (Values are the extracted values; each bracketed record id is the study reporting that value and is cited as \cite{<id>}.)

Sub-theme 'Hydropower, hydrokinetic and geothermal' of group 1: 14 studies, cite as \cite{R0007,R0110,R0111,R0167,R0296,R0424,R0475,R0544,R0816,R0885,R0911,R1450,R1468,R1837}. Methods: empirical case study 4; qualitative social study 4; literature review 4; modelling/simulation 2. Settings: sectors: power-generation-SIN 9; non-interconnected-zones 3; agriculture 1; industry 1 | departments: Huila 2; Chocó 1; Boyacá 1; Antioquia 1; Caldas 1; none stated 8. Technical outcomes: Savonius turbine 1 m2 gives ~142 W and 1245 kWh/y [R0424]; Sinú 1 kW turbine average efficiency 0.5359 [R0111]; gravitational vortex turbine 0.01-20 kW, mean efficiency 54% [R1468]; pump-turbine delivery 0.7936 l/s [R0007]; 115 small hydro plants with 867.31 MW effective capacity [R0885]; rewinding raised minimum breakdown voltage from 38.4 to 95.6 kV [R0475]; dry climate cuts hydropower about 10% by 2050 [R0167]; geothermal 793 MW installed by 2050 in the best scenario [R0816]; geothermal pilot peaked at 77 kWe [R1450]; Nereidas-1 well recorded 200 °C [R1837]. Economic outcomes: avoided electricity cost COP 12,146,112/yr and payback 3 years 3 months [R0007]; winding failure would cost 14-28 million USD vs ~1.7 million USD for rewinding [R0475]; GDP growth reduced up to 0.28% by dry climate [R0167]; geothermal cost 5.16 million USD/MW [R0816]; reservoir spill valued at 2.5 billion COP [R1468]. Environmental outcomes: El Quimbo flooded over 8,500 ha and displaced about 1,500 people [R0110]; about 23,675 people displaced by about 30% of installed capacity [R0544]; 59% of hearing speakers opposed the small hydro project [R0911]; emissions cut about 94% versus oil generation [R0424]; geothermal carbon footprint cut 19% (OFA) and 11% (OFB) [R1450]; 58.2 t CO2/MWh avoided in the best geothermal scenario [R0816]; acceptance of geothermal electricity 84.72% [R0296]. Pattern: Large and small hydropower evidence is dominated by social conflict and territorial displacement (R0110, R0544, R0911) while small-scale hydrokinetic and vortex turbines (R0424, R0111, R1468) show only site-scale potential, and geothermal remains at scenario and pilot level (R0816, R1450), so the group agrees on environmental-social costs more than on technical performance. (Values are the extracted values; each bracketed record id is the study reporting that value and is cited as \cite{<id>}.)

Sub-theme 'Electric-vehicle fleet transition, life-cycle emissions and cost (road and river)' of group 4: 8 studies, cite as \cite{R0031,R0130,R0168,R0193,R0260,R0421,R1813,R0896}. Technical outcomes: EV vs ICEV taxi 16.67 vs 122.38 kWh/100 km [R0193]; about 4,318 charging points needed by 2050 [R0260]; ~2,140 chargers by 2030 and ~9,850 by 2040 [R0168]; AFVs 52.7% of fleet by 2050 [R0260]; Scenario 2 (about 50% hybrids) cuts energy use 24.64% (2035) and 33.81% (2040) [R0130]; TRL 9 for battery, TRL 7 for hydrogen [R0896]. Economic outcomes: EV 52.13% cheaper after 20 years [R0193]; 0.03 vs 0.07 USD/km [R0193]; accumulated cost 51,498.69 vs 108,203.09 USD [R0193]; without incentives EV cost +12.94% [R0193]; full passenger-transport electrification by 2050 cuts costs 40% [R1813]; 600,000 EVs in 2030 cut 3.5% [R1813]; ~1,070 direct jobs by 2030 and 4,925 by 2040 [R0168]. Environmental outcomes: BEV GWP 27.79%, 18.25%, 13.02% lower than petrol, diesel, natural gas cars but 9.01% above diesel bus [R0421]; battery propulsion with renewable electricity cut GWP 92.6% versus petrol [R0031]; with coal-only electricity battery GWP exceeds petrol [R0031]; 27.40 vs 217.75 g CO2/km [R0193]; CO2eq -14.6% and PM -20.3% by 2050 (BAU) [R0260]; CO2 savings 32,100 t (2030) and 147,750 t (2040) [R0168]; El Niño raises emissions up to 38%, La Niña lowers them 14% [R1813].
